producer_report.summary:
`athena land --pr` now pushes the job's own landing commit (found by its Athena-Job and Athena-Verified-Content trailers) to `athena/<job>`. That commit already has the trailers and the records, so every commit on the branch passes `athena check --history`. The earlier code pushed the bare candidate plus a records-only commit, which caused the two violations on PR #39. Both the old commit-building code and its tests are removed.

Rerunning on a job whose PR is still open now also checks the branch head, again by looking for the landing commit:
- If the remote head already equals the landing commit, nothing is pushed.
- If the landing commit descends from the remote head, a plain push advances it.
- Otherwise (for example PR #39's bare candidate) the head is replaced by a forced push. A new guard, `check_replace`, allows this only on `athena/<job>`. `Git::push_replace` re-reads the remote head just before pushing and refuses if it moved.

The stored PR number is kept and its stored head is updated. `open_pr` is not called again. A PR that is merged or no longer open is left alone. Merging is still off by default.

I added unit tests in `gh.rs`, `pr.rs` and `athena-git`. A lifecycle test uses a real repo and a bare remote. It sets up an open PR whose branch holds the bare candidate and shows that `check_history` reports violations on it. After the rerun the branch head is the landed commit, PR #39 is reused with no new PR, and `check_history` is clean. A second rerun changes nothing.

The design doc, `docs/decisions.md` (new D87) and `CHANGELOG.md` record the chosen approach, the rejected alternatives and the reason. Those alternatives are a bare candidate with rewritten trailers, a synthetic records commit, and closing the PR to open a new one.

The force is not a native compare-and-swap push, because the flag's name contains a word the boundary scan forbids. The check and the push are two git calls, so a push by someone else in that gap is not excluded by git itself. D87 states this."

checks_run.note: run before the last one-line test fix; the final edit only changed a test string
all suites pass, including the new gh.rs, athena-git, pr.rs and lifecycle tests

open_issues: The force is plain `+commit:ref`, not a native compare-and-swap push. `Git::push_replace` re-reads the remote head right before pushing and refuses if it moved, but a push by someone else in that gap is not excluded by git. A true compare-and-swap push needs a flag whose name the boundary scan forbids. D87 records the gap.
The user still has to rerun `athena land --pr` on job 20261013-150709-b67z to repair PR #39. The job's landing commit must be reachable from local HEAD.
Older CHANGELOG entries still say the pushed branch is the candidate plus a records commit, and that the push is never forced. I left them as history. The new Fixed entry and D87 supersede them.
The brief listed run.rs as a deliverable, but I did not need to change it.
mistakes: A first unit test used the job id 'never', which JobId rejects. I fixed it to a well-formed id.
Python and heredocs are denied, so I made the edits with the Edit tool. That is slower, but it caused no errors.
learnings: The outcome record cannot hold the landing commit's own hash, because the commit contains the record. The landed commit is therefore found by trailers: newest commit on local HEAD with Athena-Job: <id> and Athena-Verified-Content. Only landing commits carry Athena-Verified-Content.

git remote get-url expands url.<base>.insteadOf. A test cannot point a github.com origin at a bare repo that way, so the lifecycle test builds LandPr with GitRemote naming the bare repo's path directly.
Job ids must match YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-xxxx, even in tests.
run.rs needed no change because Finished.landed_commit already exists.
desires: A way to read a saved tool-output file, or to run a test with the output filtered, without the pipes the sandbox rules forbid.
Permission to name a git compare-and-swap push flag in source. The boundary scan rejects the word it contains.
